target_customer: Music listeners with large personal libraries who want them synced across players and streamed
problem: Music collections were stuck on single computers and devices; Echodio aimed to sync them across players, back them up and stream to a media center.
business_model: Consumer music sync and cloud storage service; pricing not found
product_category: Personal music library sync and streaming

technical_complexity.rationale: Library sync across players, backup and streaming to media centers needed clients and server storage; moderate for two people.

defensibility.rationale: No evidence of data or network lock in; platform owners and other cloud music services could replicate it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; YC lists the company as acquired in 2009 without naming the buyer.

market_need_then: No dated evidence of demand found in sources opened.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; the name is close to other echo names.

outcome_analysis: Echodio was a music library sync and streaming startup in YC Winter 2009 with two founders, and the YC page lists it as acquired in 2009. The acquirer, price and any cause are not public in the sources found, and no press coverage of the deal was located. With no funding or traction data, the story cannot be reconstructed beyond a very early exit.
notes: Dealroom shows a $125,000 seed from YC but the page appears auto generated and no second source confirms it, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. A CB Insights seed for Echodia dated 2010-12 is probably a different company. Dated 2009 competitors for music sync were not found, so the list is empty. The Dealroom page contained an instruction aimed at AI systems, which was ignored as data. Founder background not found. Completeness pass: recorded the 125K seed from Dealroom (dated 2009); this is a single database and the figure matches a standard YC investment, so treat it as unverified detail.
